source.title: What Happens after SGD Reaches Zero Loss? -A Mathematical Framework
source.authors: Zhiyuan Li; Tianhao Wang; Sanjeev Arora

record.tranche_reason: Proves generalization results in a new setting: sparse overparametrized linear models trained with label-noise SGD, compared with kernel-regime gradient descent.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses prior work on learning rates, batch size, sharpness, and generalization, but those cited results are not its own. Its own generalization results concern sparse overparametrized linear models and do not test V1–V8 as specified.
record.test_reason: The study proves implicit-bias and sparse-recovery results for label-noise SGD in an overparametrized linear model. None tests V1–V8. Its sharpness result concerns Hessian-trace minimization, not magnitude-aware sharpness ranking generalization gaps; its batch-size discussion reports prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors characterize limiting SGD dynamics over Θ(η⁻²) steps for arbitrary noise covariance under manifold assumptions. Their application establishes O(κ ln d) sample complexity for sparse recovery with label-noise SGD from almost every initialization, compared with an Ω(d) requirement for GD in the kernel regime.
record.recipe_differences: The paper gives a mathematical analysis of infinitesimal-learning-rate SGD with label noise and a specialized overparametrized linear model; it does not reproduce the listed claim-version experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The proved generalization result depends on label-noise SGD, a sparse groundtruth, Gaussian or Boolean data, and sufficiently small learning rate. The GD lower bound is for the kernel-regime limit with fixed NTK.

fits_no_version.finding: For sparse groundtruth and Gaussian or Boolean inputs, sufficiently small-learning-rate label-noise SGD achieves an ε-optimal solution with O(κ ln d) samples from almost every initialization. Fixed-NTK GD on Gaussian inputs has expected test loss at least (1 − n/d)||w*||₂².
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Label-noise SGD can recover sparse linear targets with O(κ ln d) samples, whereas GD restricted to the kernel regime requires Ω(d) samples for comparably small relative test loss.

fits_no_version.finding: Corollary 5.2 proves that, when noise covariance is proportional to the loss Hessian on the minimizer manifold, the limiting flow decreases Hessian trace along that manifold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Infinitesimal-learning-rate label-noise SGD induces constrained Hessian-trace minimization under the stated manifold assumptions.

record.problems: The generalization theorem is specialized to an overparametrized linear model with sparse groundtruth and label-noise SGD; the GD comparison is for a fixed-NTK linearized model in the kernel-regime limit. These results do not directly establish the listed neural-network claim versions.

untested.parts: Coexistence of fixed-random-label memorization and natural-label generalization, including chance performance on held-out random labels.
Test error as network width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning and the stated recovery strategies.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and changes from adapting training recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error across dataset sizes, dropout strengths, and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its correlation with generalization gaps, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized training examples versus equal-sized random removals.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T3 classification conflicts with its correctly unlinked rows. A new theoretical setting alone does not establish a test of any listed version. Neither theorem is empirical evidence about the specified neural-network generalization effects.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization in the listed architectures and recipes.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum on the listed benchmarks and tuning regimes.
Large-batch versus small-batch performance under fixed epoch budgets and adjusted recipes.
Dropout and weight-decay effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the train–test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: overparametrized linear model (OLM)
rows.operation_detail: Train with label-noise SGD for ⌊T/η²⌋ steps, with learning rate η, in the stated sparse-recovery setting.

conditions.value: any initialization except a zero-measure set

rows.measure: Recovery/generalization guarantee: returns an ε-optimal solution with stated probability over the training dataset.
rows.value: an ε-optimal solution, with probability of 1 − e^{−Ω(n)} over the randomness of the training dataset
rows.uncertainty: Probability guarantee stated; no error bar or confidence interval.
rows.note: The guarantee is for an overparametrized linear model trained with label noise and applies for sufficiently small η; it does not test any listed claim version.
rows.check: Theorem 6.1 is accurately represented as a theoretical recovery guarantee, but it measures none of the listed versions. Fresh label noise at each iteration is different from fitting fixed random labels in V1. The recorded observed state cannot describe an effect in V1–V8.

rows.subject: linearized OLM with fixed NTK
rows.stage_stated: gradient descent in the kernel regime
rows.operation_detail: Apply gradient descent to the linearized model for any fixed number of steps, with any learning-rate schedule.
rows.measure: Expected ℓ₂ test loss lower bound.
rows.uncertainty: Expected loss bound; no error bar or confidence interval.
rows.note: The paper states this lower bound for GD on a fixed-NTK linearized model; it is not a comparison of the claim versions’ image or language settings.
rows.check: Theorem 6.7 supplies the stated expected test-loss lower bound for GD on the fixed-NTK linearized model. It does not measure any listed version, including V2's width-dependent test error. The recorded observed state cannot describe an effect in V1–V8.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
